nodes.cluster: C2 — identity vs label (content identity primitives inventory)
nodes.title: No canonical tree-digest algorithm exists, and a naive one produces false drift on CRLF
nodes.problem: There is no shared, canonical, cross-platform tree-digest routine. Measured trap: hashing raw bytes over the same file list on the two sides gives DIFFERENT digests (working tree e143c9c3… vs installed 64cd947c…) purely because 34 text files are CRLF in the git checkout and LF in the installed payload. Any identity primitive must normalise line endings on UTF-8-decodable files and pass binaries through untouched (14 of the payload files are binary: .png, .pyd, .ttf — a naive replace corrupts them and produces false mismatches).
nodes.evidence: Measured on this host: 1805 shared files; 1771 byte-identical; 34 differ only by CRLF (raw digest MISMATCH: e143c9c3… vs 64cd947c…); 1 genuinely differs (the pypanel). Normalised (CRLF->LF on UTF-8 decodable files only) the digests agree on all 1804 shared-and-matching files. Cost measured: full-tree sha256 0.264 s / 98.4 MB / 1972 files; .py-only 0.166 s / 1552 files; both sides 0.236-0.244 s for the 1805-file subset.

nodes.problem: The harness Jev client discards the effective model the API reports. The SDK response carries model='the model used to answer the request'; the harness writes only the requested 'jev-latest'. A tier decision routed by a Jev that was actually served by a different model is indistinguishable from one served by the requested model.
nodes.evidence: jev_client.py:100-110 _answers_to_dict copies choices/scores/nouls/request_id and never touches resp.model; :140 sets model = model or questions['model'] ('jev-latest', questions.json:4); :152 ledgers {"model": model}. The product adapter validates the same field against _REPORTED_MODEL (python/synapse/jev/adapter.py:154-157) and ledgers reported_model (adapter.py:353). The harness ledger therefore cannot tell 'jev-latest was served' from 'jev-latest was requested'.

nodes.cluster: C4-install — installed-tree integrity (installer, installation.json, payload manifest, runtime drift detection)
nodes.title: Add an installed-tree identity/drift check to the runtime doctor
nodes.problem: No runtime surface ever re-derives the installed tree's integrity. The drift verdict exists only inside the maintenance CLI (engine.verify -> verify_runtime, engine.py:517), which the product never calls and no artist runs. A check the running system can produce and surface (doctor is the shipped diagnostic surface: python/synapse/server/doctor.py:1050 run_doctor, surfaced by the panel's Doctor button at python/synapse/panel/synapse_panel.py:1278 and panel/doctor_dialog.py:121) does not exist. A new check 'installed_tree' should compare the manifest-listed files of the active runtime against the manifest already shipped inside the tree (payload-manifest.json) and report the drifted file names, with the files-map digest as the cheap headline.
nodes.evidence: installer/synapse_setup/engine.py:68-80 defines verify_runtime; engine.py:437 calls it at install; engine.py:517 re-runs it inside engine.verify(). Live run of the shipped front door: C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Programs/SYNAPSE-5.97.6/maintenance/python/python.exe -I setup_cli.py verify --app C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Programs/SYNAPSE-5.97.6 → {"status": "FAIL", "error": "Installed file check failed: houdini/python_panels/synapse_panel.pypanel", "exception": "SetupError"}. The capability is present and correct; the defect is that it is reachable only by hand (Start-menu entry at installer/windows/Synapse.iss:57) and its FAIL never reaches the artist, the panel, the doctor, or the server.

nodes.cluster: C4-install — installed-tree integrity (installer, installation.json, payload manifest, runtime drift detection)
nodes.title: Make the installation receipt carry the tree's content identity, not just a check summary
nodes.problem: The per-file identity of the installed tree has no canonical, cheap, quotable carrier. The per-file map exists (payload-manifest.json + installation.json.runtimes[active].files) but a consumer wanting 'is this tree the tree we installed?' must re-hash 1972 files (0.224 s) or reimplement digest conventions. The installer should compute and record a single tree identity (files-map digest 81ab387bd7d86dea, plus payload_id) in installation.json and in ~/.synapse/install_stamp.json, so the runtime can compare a stored value against a recomputed one in one comparison, and so 'the installed tree changed' is a state change with a timestamp rather than an inference.
nodes.evidence: installer/synapse_setup/engine.py:437 (checks = verify_runtime(runtime, manifest)), :442 (state['runtimes'][str(runtime)] = manifest), :472 (registrations[].sha256), :475-482 (stamp{path,sha256,original}), :483 (state['checks'] = checks). Live installation.json: checks={'files_checked': 1972, 'status': 'PASS', 'xml': 'PASS'}, one registration (packages/synapse.json, de23d2c2...), stamp with path/sha256/original. The receipt already carries the full per-file map, so the fix is to promote ONE derived value (files-map digest + payload_id) into the receipt and the stamp rather than leaving every consumer to re-derive it, and to make that value the cross-surface identity both sides can quote.

nodes.cluster: C4-install — installed-tree integrity (installer, installation.json, payload manifest, runtime drift detection)
nodes.title: Classify host-mutable interface assets so a drift verdict is sound, not noisy
nodes.problem: A naive drift check would report a false positive on the one file Houdini is designed to rewrite in place. The installer already owns a whitelist concept for user-owned pref files (engine.py:155-160 authorized_pref_file), but there is no equivalent list for HOST-MUTATED files inside the installed tree. The drift verdict must classify houdini/python_panels/synapse_panel.pypanel and houdini/toolbar/synapse.shelf (Houdini rewrites these in place when the artist registers them) separately from genuine tampering, and must tolerate the 474 legitimate non-manifest files (pycache, .synapse/agent_health_history.jsonl) without flagging them.
nodes.evidence: installer/synapse_setup/registration.py:8-14 UI_CORE maps 'houdini/python_panels/synapse_panel.pypanel' -> pref destination 'python_panels/synapse_panel.pypanel', and the installed tree's houdini/ subtree is on HOUDINI_PATH via hpath (registration.py:38) — so the mutable copy inside the content-addressed tree is the one Houdini loads. The drifted file's diff against the repo copy is exactly the includeInPaneTabMenu + ASCII-only signature of Houdini's own .pypanel files (8 sampled under C:/Program Files/Side Effects Software/Houdini 22.0.400/houdini/python_panels/: nonascii=0, 7/8 with includeInPaneTabMenu). Also 474 non-manifest files exist in the tree (473 __pycache__/*.pyc + .synapse/agent_health_history.jsonl written by python/synapse/panel/agent_health.py:185 into $SYNAPSE_ROOT/.synapse/), so a strict tree==manifest predicate would false-positive on a clean machine.

nodes.cluster: C4-install — installed-tree integrity (installer, installation.json, payload manifest, runtime drift detection)
nodes.title: Bring the source-install path up to the same install-state contract as the installer
nodes.problem: The source-install path writes a stamp with a different shape and no manifest at all, so a drift check that assumes the installer receipt exists will report UNKNOWN/false-fail for source installs. The two install paths must agree on what the seat's 'installed tree' is and on what the stamp asserts, so one drift check can serve both without a special case per path.
nodes.evidence: scripts/install_synapse_package.py:112 STAMP_NAME, :116-118 stamp_path(), :132-143 write_stamp() (schema synapse_install_stamp/v1, synapse_version, repo_root, installed_at, targets), :504 verify() (probe-based checks only). No per-file manifest is produced on this path (grep 'manifest|sha256' over the file → no hits). The two install paths therefore leave the seat with two different install states and one stamp schema whose content differs by path, so 'the installed tree' is not a single well-defined object across install methods.

adjacent_findings.title: A MAP seat can mislabel its own cluster and the board has no guard against it
adjacent_findings.found: 2026-10-22, by the recorder while extracting the candidate graph from wf_d1494930-f0c
adjacent_findings.evidence: Four of the five MAP seats returned a `cluster` string that does not match the cluster they were briefed on, in two clean swap pairs: seat attest:map:C1-carriers (briefed CLUSTER C1 - the version carrier graph) reported 'C2 - identity vs label', and seat attest:map:C2-identity (briefed CLUSTER C2) reported 'C1 - the version carrier graph'; seat attest:map:C4-install (briefed CLUSTER C4) reported 'C5-harness', and seat attest:map:C5-harness (briefed CLUSTER C5) reported 'C4-install'. Only attest:map:C3-provenance matched. The node id prefixes follow the mislabel, not the brief: the C1-carriers seat numbered its nodes C2-N1..C2-N6.
adjacent_findings.mechanism: MAP_SCHEMA.cluster is `{ type: 'string' }` - free text, no enum, and the seat prompt never asks the seat to echo the cluster id it was given. The seat's content is CORRECT (each seat's findings match the brief it received); only the self-declared label is wrong.
adjacent_findings.consequence: Any consumer that groups the map reports by the reported `cluster` field, or that parses the node-id prefix as a cluster name, will attribute findings to the wrong cluster. The first extraction attempt by this recorder did exactly that and produced a false 3-node dependency cycle (C2-N1 -> C2-N3 -> C2-N4 -> C2-N1) that does not exist - it was an artifact of conflating two different seats' N1/N3/N4.
adjacent_findings.fix_direction: Make the cluster identity structural rather than self-asserted: give the schema a `cluster_id` enum of the five known cluster ids, or better, have the recorder key the reports by the seat label (which the dispatcher controls) and treat the seat's `cluster` string as a label to be CHECKED against the brief rather than trusted.
adjacent_findings.note: This is the same defect class the board exists to catch, one level up: identity carried by an ambient label instead of a verified fact. The board's own first consumer of a seat's self-declared identity was fooled by it.
